1.title: By the Will of God
1.context: Paul signs himself an apostle by the will of God, grounded in the promise of life in Christ Jesus. The farewell letter opens with authority and hope in one breath.
1.question: What work in front of you is held by promise rather than by your own grip?

1.title: My Beloved Child
1.context: The first letter called Timothy a true child in the faith; this one calls him a beloved child, and mercy again stands between grace and peace. The framing reflection on what the greeting does not say rides this scene.
1.question: Who has called you beloved, and what did that make possible in you?

2.title: Night and Day in My Prayers
2.context: Paul thanks the God of his forefathers, served with a clear conscience, while remembering Timothy night and day. Gratitude opens this letter where command opened the first.
2.question: Whose name comes up in your prayers night and day, and have you told them?

2.title: Recalling Your Tears
2.context: The letter keeps only the parting tears and Paul's longing, not the time or place of the parting itself. Joy, for Paul here, has a meeting attached to it.
2.question: When has being missed by someone strengthened you for hard work?

2.title: The Faith That Dwelt First
2.context: Lois and Eunice are named only here in the New Testament; Acts mentions Timothy's believing mother without naming her. Dwelt is a household word: the faith lived at home in them first. The reflection on sincere faith rides this scene.
2.question: Whose home did your faith live in before it lived in you?

3.title: Fan into Flame
3.context: The gift came through the laying on of Paul's hands. Fanning is tending, and the spirit God gave is named against fear: power, love, and self-control.
3.question: What gift in you has banked down under ash, and what would fanning it look like this week?

3.title: Do Not Be Ashamed
3.context: The danger named is shame, not pain: of the testimony, and of the prisoner who carries it. Suffering is to be joined in company, by the power of God.
3.question: Where is shame, rather than fear of pain, the thing holding you back?

3.title: Before Time Began
3.context: Salvation and calling rest on God's purpose and grace granted before time began, then revealed in the appearing of Christ Jesus, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light.
3.question: What does it change that grace was granted before you could earn or lose it?

3.title: I Know Whom I Have Believed
3.context: Earlier charges had Timothy guarding God's deposit; here Paul's own deposit is guarded by God. Both directions stand in the letter series, and Paul's confidence rests on the one believed, not the strength of his grip.
3.question: What have you entrusted to God that you keep trying to guard yourself?

4.title: Hold On to the Pattern
4.context: Sound teaching has a pattern Timothy heard, held with faith and love, and the treasure is guarded with the help of the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.
4.question: What part of guarding well is actually yours to do, and what part is help you receive?

4.title: Everyone in Asia Has Deserted Me
4.context: Asia, the province of Ephesus and of Paul's longest ministry, turned away in the letter's total wording, and Phygelus and Hermogenes are named. Nothing else is known of the two men.
4.question: How do you keep working when the report from ground you loved is desertion?

4.title: He Searched Until He Found Me
4.context: Onesiphorus refreshed Paul often, was unashamed of the chains, and searched diligently in Rome until he found the prisoner. Paul answers with a mercy prayer for his household and for him on that day. His Ephesus service, known to Timothy, rides this scene.
4.question: Who needs you to search for them rather than wait to be found?

5.title: Entrust to Faithful Men
5.context: Four generations stand in one sentence: Paul, Timothy, faithful men, and those they will teach. What Timothy heard among many witnesses is handed on by entrusting, not by keeping.
5.question: What have you received that is meant to be entrusted onward, and to whom?

5.title: Soldier, Athlete, Farmer
5.context: Three ordinary trades give the ministry its shape: the soldier unentangled to please the one who enlisted him, the competitor crowned only by the rules, the farmer eating after the work.
5.question: Which of the three pictures presses on your life most right now, and why?

5.title: The Lord Will Give You Insight
5.context: Paul leaves the images unexplained and promises insight from the Lord instead. Timothy is trusted to consider, the posture of the unashamed workman the letter is forming.
5.question: What have you been told to consider that you keep asking to have explained instead?

6.title: Chained Like a Criminal
6.context: The remembrance is Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David. The apostle is chained like a criminal; the word of God is not chained, the letter's sharpest contrast.
6.question: What limit on you right now is real, and what has it not actually limited?

6.title: For the Sake of the Elect
6.context: Endurance here has an aim: that the elect may obtain the salvation in Christ Jesus with eternal glory. Suffering is measured by who it gathers, not by what it proves.
6.question: Whose future good makes your present endurance worth it?

6.title: If We Died with Him
6.context: A trustworthy saying in four lines: died and live, endure and reign, deny and be denied, faithless and he remains faithful, for he cannot deny himself. The warning and the comfort are one saying.
6.question: Which line of the four do you most need to hear as promise, and which as warning?

7.title: An Unashamed Workman
7.context: Word quarrels succeed only at ruining listeners. Against them stands the workman who accurately handles the word of truth, diligently presenting himself approved to God.
7.question: What would cutting straight look like in the words you handle this week?

7.title: Spread Like Gangrene
7.context: Empty chatter leads to more ungodliness and spreads like gangrene. Hymenaeus is named in both Timothy letters; Philetus only here. Their error, that the resurrection has already occurred, was undermining some believers' faith.
7.question: What talk in your world spreads quietly and rots what it touches?

7.title: The Firm Foundation
7.context: The foundation bears a two-sided seal: the Lord knows those who are his, and everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from iniquity. Knowledge on God's side, duty on ours.
7.question: Which side of the seal do you lean on, and which side do you avoid?

8.title: Vessels of Gold and Clay
8.context: A large house runs on vessels of gold, silver, wood, and clay. Cleansing moves a person toward honorable use: sanctified, useful to the Master, prepared for every good work.
8.question: What cleansing would make you more useful to the Master of the house?

8.title: Flee and Pursue
8.context: Fleeing youthful passions is half the motion; the pursuit of righteousness, faith, love, and peace runs together with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
8.question: What are you fleeing that needs a pursuit and a company to replace it?

8.title: Gently Reprove
8.context: The Lord's servant must not be quarrelsome but kind, able to teach, forbearing, gently reproving opponents in the hope God grants repentance. The opponent is pictured as a captive to free, not an enemy to crush.
8.question: Who opposes you that you could start treating as a captive to free?

9.title: Lovers of Themselves
9.context: The last days are described by their people, a long list in which love bends inward toward self, money, and pleasure. Paul gives Timothy the frame without naming its later referents.
9.question: Which item on the list is most ordinary in your world, and what does ordinary do to it?

9.title: A Form of Godliness
9.context: The form of godliness with its power denied is the passage's religious center: households entered quietly, the burdened captivated, always learning and never arriving at a knowledge of the truth.
9.question: Where have you settled for the form of something real while its power went missing?

9.title: Jannes and Jambres
9.context: Exodus does not name Pharaoh's magicians; Jannes and Jambres are the names tradition attached to them, used here the way Jude used tradition about Moses. Their advance has a stated limit: their folly will be plain to everyone.
9.question: What opposition are you facing that has a shorter run than it claims?

10.title: You Have Observed
10.context: Timothy followed Paul's teaching, conduct, and sufferings at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra, towns the Acts account also traces. The verdict on the persecutions is deliverance: the Lord rescued me from all of them.
10.question: Whose observed life, up close and costly, taught you more than their words?

10.title: Continue in What You Have Learned
10.context: Both movements run at once: the godly persecuted, impostors going from bad to worse. Timothy's anchors are what he learned, from whom he learned it, and the Scriptures known from infancy.
10.question: When pressure mounts, which of your anchors do you actually reach for?

10.title: God-Breathed
10.context: All Scripture is God-breathed and useful for instruction, conviction, correction, and training in righteousness, so that the man of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work.
10.question: Which of the four workings of Scripture do you welcome least, and what might it be equipping you for?

11.title: In the Presence of God
11.context: The charge is sworn before God and Christ Jesus, judge of the living and the dead, in view of his appearing and his kingdom. No command in the letter carries heavier witnesses.
11.question: What order in your life would change if you gave it before that court?

11.title: In Season and Out of Season
11.context: Preach the word, prepared in season and out: reprove, rebuke, and encourage, with every form of patient instruction. Correction and comfort are both named duties.
11.question: Which of the three, reprove, rebuke, encourage, do you drop first, and why?

11.title: Itching Ears
11.context: The stated future: hearers who will not tolerate sound doctrine gather teachers to suit their own desires and turn aside to myths. Paul names no date and no people for it.
11.question: Where do you shop for teaching that suits your desires?

11.title: Fulfill Your Ministry
11.context: Sober in all things, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill your ministry. The whole assignment, not its comfortable parts, is the standard.
11.question: What part of your assignment have you quietly left unfulfilled?

12.title: Poured Out
12.context: A drink offering was poured out entirely at the altar. Departure is a traveler's word, the striking of a tent: Paul states his expectation plainly, the time is at hand.
12.question: What would you do differently if you treated your season as a pouring rather than a storing?

12.title: Fought, Finished, Kept
12.context: Fight, race, and guarded faith, all in finished tenses. The apostle who charged others with the deposit reports his own keeping of it as done.
12.question: What would you need to be able to say is finished, not just started?

12.title: The Crown of Righteousness
12.context: The BSB breaks the sentence at its dash, and the telling keeps the fragments separate: the crown awarded by the righteous Judge on that day, and the widening promise to all who crave his appearing.
12.question: Do you crave the appearing, or mainly fear it, and what makes the difference?

13.title: Only Luke Is with Me
13.context: Demas deserted, in love of this world; Crescens and Titus are gone on assignment. Only Luke, the beloved physician of the Colossians letter, remains with Paul.
13.question: Who has stayed with you when others went, and do they know what that meant?

13.title: The Cloak and the Parchments
13.context: Mark is summoned in this same stretch of requests and pronounced useful, the Acts breach repaired by a single sentence. The cloak at Troas, the scrolls, and especially the parchments are a real man's needs before winter. Tychicus's errand to Ephesus rides this scene.
13.question: What ordinary need of yours have you been treating as too small to ask for?

13.title: Alexander the Coppersmith
13.context: Paul names an Alexander in the first letter to Timothy as well; this letter does not say whether they are the same man. Repayment is left to the Lord; Timothy's part is watchfulness.
13.question: What repayment are you holding that the letter would have you hand to the Lord?

13.title: The Lord Stood by Me
13.context: At the first defense everyone deserted, and Paul answers with forgiveness: may it not be charged against them. The Lord stood by him, the message was fully proclaimed, and the rescue confession closes over his future.
13.question: When everyone left, who stood by you, and how did that change the outcome?

13.title: Before Winter
13.context: Greetings run to Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus; Erastus remained at Corinth and Trophimus was left sick in Miletus. The deadline is human: come before winter. The close divides its gifts, the Lord with Timothy's spirit, grace with them all.
13.question: What is your before-winter thing, the visit or call that cannot wait for a better season?
